title: Playing for dancers, listeners and jazz festivals
summary: He projects more for a seated audience and looks forward to playing the jazz festival.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: We were talking about people dancing, dancing, dancing. Did you like playing for people dancing, or for people sitting down? Did you like it?
Well, if the club, if the club was in that kind of way where people sit down and listen, fine. But if it was a dancing club, I like them to dance. But if it was a sitting down audience, fine too.
Did you play differently for a sit down audience?

No, same way. I think for a sit down audience, you would have to be a little more projective. You'd have to project a little bit more. And then whereas for dancing people, you know, people would be more interested in dancing. So, it was just, you know, you didn't have to project as much. You know, you have to do your job, but you don't have to project as something to look at. Whereas with you, you know, people looking at you, sitting down, then you have to keep them interested in looking and listening. Whereas the dancing. Or a jazz festival. Yeah. Oh, a jazz festival. I love it. That's one, that's one, I look forward to playing a jazz festival every year. Because first of all, it's a, your audience will be people who come there to see you. Right. This is what I like, you know. And every year, I get people from all over the world, see. And I love it. I got my, I sent my contract back yesterday. Oh, yeah.
